parole.testo: Borrowed from Ingrian inkeroin. Equivalent to Inkeri (“Ingria”) + -oinen.

parole.testo: Attested in the Kalevala, probably originally a name as attested such in other folk poetry. According to Julius Krohn, it might originally be an Ingrian vernacular form of Russian Добрыня (Dobrynja). Variants, such as Tuurituinen and Tuurikki, are also attested.
